Diego / Marissa —

Quick read-through and suggested approach below. I kept the redline narrowly tailored to pricing mechanics so we don't concede broader commercial terms. Key principles: limit term exposure, define triggers, and preserve our ability to revert to list pricing for extraordinary cost events.

Suggested redline excerpts (high-level summary you can paste into a PDF):
1) Minimum Commitment (Floor) — The parties agree a provisional minimum charge for the first three (3) months equal to 50% of the committed monthly token volume at the agreed unit price. Any shortfall between actual usage and the provisional minimum shall be credited as a one-time invoice adjustment in the subsequent billing month.

2) Price Increase Cap — Redwood may increase per-unit fees no more than eight percent (8%) in any consecutive twelve (12) month period. Any proposed increase shall be communicated in writing 60 days in advance and is subject to mutual review if the customer provides evidence of material, sustained cloud-cost reductions.

3) Split-Tier Discount Interaction — For avoidance of doubt, committed volumes counted toward floor calculations shall be treated as applied credits for tier qualification purposes only for the first contract year. Actual tiered discounts will be applied to invoiced consumption after true-up.

4) True-up and Invoicing — True-up calculations shall occur quarterly; adjustments will be netted on the next invoice. One-time credits for floor shortfalls will not alter historical tier qualification for prior quarters.

5) Sunset / Review Clause — After month six (6) either party may request a joint commercial review to adjust floors or cap mechanics; if both parties agree, changes will be memorialized in a written amendment.

I recommend we offer the 3-month partial-credit floor rather than the customer's hard 6-month floor; it's defensible commercially and limits downside.

If you want, I can mark up their PDF and return a Dieg0_Counter_Redline.pdf (I'll send a clean copy).

Laura Bennett

Ran the model against Acme's forecast. High level:
- If we accept Laura's 3-month 50% provisional floor, expected net revenue over first 12 months decreases by ~3.2% vs. current draft (customer 6-month hard floor).
- The 8% cap on increases has negligible immediate impact; it mainly reduces our optionality in year 2+ if cloud costs spike, but we can rely on the extraordinary-cost carveout Laura mentioned.
- Split-tier interaction language as suggested preserves our ability to apply volume discounts post-true-up; worst-case margin erosion comes from sustained underspend under the floor during year one.

Recommendation: approve Laura's language; offer a commercial sweetener instead of a longer floor concession — propose a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the first quarter invoices if Acme signs within 10 business days. That reduces perceived risk for them without extending contractual exposure for us.
